title: Demographics of disks around young very low-mass stars and brown dwarfs in Lupus
question: Do disks around brown dwarfs and very low-mass stars in Lupus follow the demographic relations (disk mass, size, accretion) known for disks around stars?

what.value: Stellar properties (SpT, Teff, AV, L*) of targets

evidence.quote: were reported by (cite: alcala2014; alcala2017) and (cite: muzic+2014)

what.value: Band 7 fluxes and data of original Lupus disks survey

evidence.quote: For the observations results from the Lupus disks survey (ALMA Project ID: 2013.1.00220.S), we refer to (cite: ansdell+2016).

what.value: Mass accretion rates and accretion luminosities

evidence.quote: The $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{acc}}$ and its uncertainty is taken from the X-Shooter observations presented by (cite: alcala2014; alcala2017).

recipe.method: CASA calibration and Briggs-weighted continuum imaging with line-free channels
uvmodelfit with elliptical Gaussian or point source; curve of growth for resolved; rms in 4-9 arcsec annulus; upper limits 3 rms

recipe.goal: Fit visibilities with disk brightness models
recipe.method: Gaussian profile for BDs (6 parameters); Nuker profile for stellar disks (9 parameters); fit in uv plane
Radii enclosing 68% and 95% of cumulative flux from each MCMC model
Optically thin emission, constant kappa and Tdust
Linear regression with Bayesian linmix including upper limits; Anderson-Darling tests
assumptions: Gas-to-dust ratio 100 for total disk mass

evidence.quote: The total dust mass for the detected BD disks range between $0.2$ and $3.2$ $M_{\Earth}$.
the slope and intercept become $1.69 \pm 0.19$ and $-3.89 \pm 0.13$
The resulting slope is $\alpha = 0.69 \pm 0.14$, while the intercept is $\beta = -7.26 \pm 0.36$.

answer_key.quantity: Median accretion depletion timescale BDs vs stars

evidence.quote: The median value of this timescale for the BD sample is $9.5$ Myr, while for the stellar sub-sample considered is $1.4$ Myr.

answer_key.quantity: AD test probability, Mdust/Mstar BD vs stars

evidence.quote: obtaining a probability of $6 \%$ that the BD and stellar disk populations are drawn from the same distribution
with only a $0.6 \%$ probability that the BD and stellar disks populations are drawn from the same original distribution

not_stated_but_needed: Cell size and image size for tclean
Priors and bounds of the MCMC fits
Burn-in and how fit convergence was judged
Distance used for conversion of dust mass formula (exact), and Planck function details
Flux-ratio correction details for completion survey
missing_for_reproduction: Stellar masses and accretion rates from external papers
score_reason: Data are public and methods are well described, but imaging parameters and priors are missing, and the analysis relies on several external datasets.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric fluxes, dust masses and sizes in tables.
